title: Design System: dayroute — The Paper Line

micro.purpose: 11px, the system's floor. Badges, meta/address lines, footnotes — both the uppercase signage caps and a set of plain reading-adjacent lines, told apart by weight and line-height, not size.

ui-text.purpose: 13px, the most-shared step. Buttons, inputs, names, sequence numbers — both interactive/identifying UI text and reading text (sheet help, form values, the paste textarea, toasts).

sub-head.purpose: 16px. Declared for dialog titles and tight-context brand, but its one real consumer is the tray's delete glyph (×) — sheet-title and pane-title are actually set one step down, at ui-text/13px.

compact-stat.purpose: 19px. The optimisation delta figure and the day-nav prev/next chevrons — a figure and a nav glyph sharing a size coincidentally.

wordmark.purpose: 23px. The brand name; the mobile-breakpoint secondary total figure shares this size coincidentally.

secondary-lead.purpose: 27px. The desktop miles/stop-count totals beside the lead figure.

primary-lead.purpose: 39px. The driving-total lead figure on desktop — the single largest number in the system.

mono.purpose: The paste-a-list textarea (13px, on-scale, line-height 1.7 — a bare literal, not one of the three --lh- roles) and inline code (a relative 0.92em, the system's one type value outside the fixed scale).

shadows.name: pin-tick-shadow
shadows.purpose: Separates a map pin's badge from unpredictable tile colour underneath it — ink-strong at 28% alpha, hand-written since a marker has no paper ground to tonal-step against.

shadows.name: pin-stem-shadow
shadows.purpose: The same marker-separation exception applied to the pin's stem.

shadows.name: pin-label-shadow
shadows.purpose: The same exception applied to the pin's hover-revealed name label.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Default duration for ordinary state change: button/input/station hover and focus, background and colour transitions.

motion.name: t-base
motion.purpose: Toast enter animation; the arrow-travel and pin-hover transform durations.

motion.name: t-move
motion.purpose: Named duration for spatial motion; the reorder FLIP's actual hardcoded duration (460ms) sits close to but not exactly on this token, since the Web Animations API call can't read the CSS custom property.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The default easing curve — every ordinary state transition and the Optimise arrow's working-state loop.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The travel curve, reserved for things that move through space: the reorder FLIP, the arrow hover-slide, the pin/station hover-lift. Reused as an equivalent literal inside the JS-driven count-up and route draw-on, which can't reference the CSS custom property directly.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, green action in the system — Optimise. Its arrow travels on hover and loops a departing keyframe while the optimiser is genuinely working.

components.name: The Line — Track Segment
components.description: The system's signature component: a fixed station (hollow ink-strong ring) and a flexible station (green ring + filled core) joined by a green track, split into a heavy stopped segment, a solid driven segment, and a dashed slack segment — thickness itself carries meaning, proportional to real minutes. Drive-leg duration rides a chip on the driven stretch. Read straight out of schedule.js's _draw() geometry; colours here are read live via getComputedStyle in the real app, not hardcoded the way this static snippet has to be.

narrative.overview:
dayroute's thesis is unchanged by this pass: the schedule *is* the diagram, not a list beside a map. A vertical time axis (The Line) places every stop at its real clock position, so the empty space between two stations is drawn to scale and IS the drive leg. What changed is the material the diagram is printed on. The system's original world — fired enamel, midnight blue, lit by scarlet/cobalt/amber — is entirely gone, replaced at the user's explicit, direct instruction after it failed in the product's own stated use scene: read on a phone, in a car, in the sun. The direction contract embedded in index.html's <body> comment records the change plainly: "Palette replaced at the user's direction; the dark original lost to a daylight use scene." There was no fresh Impeccable direction round behind this world the way there was for the enamel one (seed 3faa1e80); the code — style.css, schedule.js, map.js — is the only design record, exactly as it was before.

The new world reads as a rail diagram printed on warm oat stock: one paper ground, cards raised to true white, one green line ink for the route and everything routine, and clay — green's complement — held to exactly one job: won't-fit and collision, never anything ordinary. The card/ground separation is not a stylistic pick; it is a measured floor. Paper Raise on Paper is 1.31:1, and that number exists in this document because the previous theme's identical step measured 1.12:1 and was reported twice, independently, as "events are the same colour as the calendar, hard to visually see." --ink-dim holds its own measured floor: 4.53:1 on paper, "the floor, not a soft grey."

Confirmed rejections, all visible in the shipped code: no shadow anywhere except the map's own markers (all three parts now, not one hack for one state), no gradient, and no stock basemap tile set (OpenFreeMap's positron style is recoloured at load by map.js's enamelise() — a function name that is now a misnomer left over from the enamel world). The chrome/diagram radius split survives untouched: tool chrome rounds at --radius-chrome (5px), the diagram and the map's own route/track stay exactly 0.
keyCharacteristics: Ground is a material, not a backdrop: warm paper throughout, cards raised to pure white at a measured, load-bearing 1.31:1 step — a floor, recorded because dropping toward the old theme's 1.12:1 is the exact failure this palette exists to fix.
Two line inks, not four: green is the route, the primary action, and a flexible station; clay is its sole complement — attention, won't-fit, and collision, never anything routine.
Both line inks carry a deepened text-only variant, because each raw value fails the 4.5:1 small-text floor on paper (green 4.13:1, clay 4.38:1): green-ink reaches 6.93:1, clay-ink reaches 5.98:1.
The Line is drawn in weighted, proportional segments, not a dot in a gap: heavy (7px) while stopped, solid (3px) while driving, dashed (3px, 2 4) across slack, proportional to real minutes.

schedule.js reads every Line colour from CSS custom properties via getComputedStyle at draw time, and app.js's legend does the same — neither hardcodes a hex, a rule earned after a prior palette swap left literals pointing at a dead theme.

Map markers are real pins — a 26px badge on a 9px stem — with a styled hover label replacing the native tooltip. box-shadow is permitted on the pin alone, because a marker floats over unpredictable tile colour and cannot separate from it by tonal step.
The basemap is Positron (light), recoloured by source luminance onto the same paper the interface is printed on.

The type scale, the 4px spacing grid, the hair/hair-wall border-weight hierarchy, the chrome/diagram radius split, and the five-value motion system all carry over from the prior build unchanged — reverified against the current code.

rules.name: The Card Floor Rule
rules.body: Paper Raise on Paper measures 1.31:1 — the separation that makes a scheduled event legibly distinct from an empty grid row. This is a floor, not a target to erode: the previous world's identical step measured 1.12:1 and was reported twice, independently, as illegible.

rules.name: The Deepened-Ink Rule
rules.body: Both line inks fail the 4.5:1 small-text floor at their raw value — green at 4.13:1, clay at 4.38:1 — so each carries a deepened, text-only sibling (green-ink 6.93:1, clay-ink 5.98:1) for every place the colour sits as text rather than a fill or a ring.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Exactly two hues carry state on the diagram and the map — green (route, flexible) and clay (won't-fit, collision) — plus ink-strong, a neutral extreme that marks a fixed appointment without being a third hue.

rules.name: The Tokenised Derivative Rule
rules.body: Every alpha wash, hover-deepened fill, or backdrop tint is a named custom property, never an inline hex or rgba() outside :root. A palette replacement leaves bare literals silently pointing at the dead theme unless every derived value is tokenised in the same pass as the primaries — this has now failed twice in this project's history.

rules.name: The Named-Role Scale Rule
rules.body: Every font size is one of the eight --fs- tokens, documented by role. A new component reaches for a role, never a bare pixel value or a ninth size.

rules.name: The Weight Carries Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: 400/600/700 mean reading text / interactive text / a leading figure-or-brand-or-badge everywhere except three named exceptions (.daynav-btn stays 400, .daynav-date stays 700, .pane-title/.sheet-title are headings deliberately downgraded to 600).

rules.name: The Three Line-Heights Rule
rules.body: --lh-tight/--lh-label/--lh-read are the complete set; the two bare-literal exceptions (the paste textarea's 1.7, the delete glyph's 1) are single-purpose optical fixes, not a fourth role.

rules.name: The 4px-Grid Rule
rules.body: Every meaningful gap, padding, and margin is one of the seven --space- steps or the --pad/--gap aliases.

rules.name: The One-Screen Rule
rules.body: Desktop never scrolls the page; only the panes scroll internally.

rules.name: The Read-Only Overlay Rule
rules.body: The Line's SVG track only ever reads geometry (getBoundingClientRect) off FullCalendar's DOM — it never sets position on .fc-v-event or info.el, because FullCalendar sizes events by absolute top/bottom to keep them proportional to duration.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Material Rule
rules.body: Depth is tonal, not cast. A surface is "above" another by sitting a lighter step of the same paper plus a hairline border — never a shadow, never a blur — everywhere except the marker exception.

rules.name: The Marker Shadow Exception
rules.body: box-shadow is permitted on .pin-tick, .pin-stem, and .pin-label alone, because a map marker sits over unpredictable tile colour and has no tonal ground to step against. It is not precedent for a shadow anywhere else.

rules.name: Chrome Radius, Diagram Stays Sharp
rules.body: Tool chrome rounds at --radius-chrome (5px); the diagram and the map's own route/track rendering stay exactly 0, with circles as their only curve.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: --hair is the default border weight everywhere; --hair-wall is reserved for major structural panel dividers, and the Line/Map seam additionally overrides its colour to --ink-dim because it is the single most important boundary in the layout.

dos: Do treat 1.31:1 (Paper Raise on Paper) as a floor, not a target to erode — a material change that brings a card and its ground closer together than this reopens the exact defect this palette exists to fix.
Do treat --green-ink (6.93:1) and --clay-ink (5.98:1) as the only legible way to set either line ink as small text; the raw values fail 4.5:1 on paper.
Do read Line and legend colours from getComputedStyle, never hardcode a hex in schedule.js or app.js's renderLegend().
Do remember map.js's route colours are literal strings, not CSS variables, and update them by hand alongside style.css on any future palette change — MapLibre's paint properties can't consume var().
Do round tool chrome at --radius-chrome (5px) and keep the diagram and the map's route/track at exactly 0.
Do reach for one of the eight named --fs- roles and one of the three --lh- line-heights, never a bare pixel value.
Do draw every gap, padding, and margin from --space-1 through --space-7 (or the --pad/--gap aliases).
Do use clay freely in chrome for anything that genuinely needs attention. The moment clay touches a station or a map pin, hold it to exactly one meaning: won't-fit or collision.
Do keep the tick, connector, and card of a station acting as one coupled object — check LABEL_INSET/margin-left before changing any one of them independently.
Do tokenise every derived alpha wash or hover fill the moment it's introduced, in the same pass as the primary it derives from.
donts: Don't add a coloured left-edge accent to a card or container.
Don't add a shadow or a gradient anywhere except the map marker's three parts (.pin-tick/.pin-stem/.pin-label).
Don't let clay mark a routine drive leg or a routine (non-unfit) station/pin state.

Don't invert .maplibregl-ctrl-group button span's filter — that convention only made sense against the enamel world's dark control glyphs; inverting it on paper renders the zoom buttons white-on-white and they disappear.
Don't invent a third hue for the Line or the map. Green, clay, and ink-strong are the complete set.
Don't add a decorative, idle-state loop. Looping animation is reserved for feedback tied to a genuinely pending operation; a pulsing now-line dot was tried and rejected for exactly this reason.
Don't give a station its own left-border or full-recolour treatment for state; state lives on .ev-name's text colour and the badge, never a card-level border swap.

Don't trust the "A station, not a card" comment above .fc-v-event — it describes the previous world's doctrine and was not updated when the rule beneath it started giving every station a real paper-raise/rule surface at rest.
Don't treat .btn--line's hover/.is-ready state (ink-strong text on green, 3.32:1) as a model to copy elsewhere — it's a recorded gap under this system's own 4.5:1 floor, not a sanctioned pairing.
